title: Cost-related care foregoing co-occurs with household financial adaptation

observations.period: 2025; any cost-related care foregoing and household adaptation

denominator.unit: respondents with complete E1_a-E1_e care-foregoing fields

observations.method: Any Yes among E1_a-E1_e defines cost-related care foregoing; outcomes are weighted single-year cross-sectional shares using weight.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate-weight standard errors in this pass; outcome fields have separate nonmissing universes.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting any of five care types skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: Shared need, prior financial scarcity, health, coverage, access, or reverse timing may produce both care foregoing and adaptation.

observations.period: 2025; no cost-related care foregoing and household adaptation

denominator.unit: respondents with complete E1_a-E1_e care-foregoing fields

observations.method: Any No across E1_a-E1_e defines no reported cost-related care foregoing; outcomes are weighted single-year cross-sectional shares using weight.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate-weight standard errors in this pass; outcome fields have separate nonmissing universes.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting no listed care type skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: No reported foregoing does not prove no unmet need, affordability, or absence of other financial pressure.

observations.period: 2025; unexpected medical-expense amount among care-foregoing respondents

denominator.unit: any-care-foregoing respondents with nonmissing E12_a amount band

observations.method: Weighted distribution of E12_a among respondents classified as any-care-foregoing; amount question is asked for unexpected major medical expenses.
observations.uncertainty: Amount is a categorical recalled range, not an exact bill or event amount; no replicate-weight standard errors in this pass.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting any of five care types skipped because of cost and a nonmissing E12_a response.
observations.counterinterpretation: The amount may concern an unexpected expense unrelated to the skipped care and does not identify the price of care not obtained.

observations.period: 2025; unexpected medical-expense amount among no-care-foregoing respondents

denominator.unit: no-care-foregoing respondents with nonmissing E12_a amount band

observations.method: Weighted distribution of E12_a among respondents classified as no-care-foregoing; amount question is asked for unexpected major medical expenses.
observations.uncertainty: Amount is a categorical recalled range, not an exact bill or event amount; no replicate-weight standard errors in this pass.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting no listed care type skipped because of cost and a nonmissing E12_a response.
observations.counterinterpretation: No reported care foregoing does not prove the unexpected expense was affordable or that it did not affect other care decisions.

boundary: Same-respondent cross-sectional co-occurrence does not establish a dated medical episode, causal direction, exact bill, alternative, care outcome, remedy, trust, or political action.
